title: Backend mid scenario connection pool exhaustion
topic: Backend mid scenario connection pool exhaustion
question: Under moderate traffic, your API starts throwing 'timeout waiting for connection from pool' errors, even though the database itself isn't overloaded. What's happening, and how do you fix it?
idealAnswer:
Identifies that all connections in the pool are tied up, likely held by the slow report query (or several concurrent instances of it) for longer than usual, starving every other request of a connection

Would check for connections not being released properly too, e.g. a code path that opens a connection and doesn't close/return it on an error path, slowly leaking pool capacity over time

Proposes fixes: adding a query timeout so a slow query can't hold a connection indefinitely, and/or moving the slow report query to a separate pool or a read replica so it can't starve the main request path

Considers pool sizing itself, but recognizes that just increasing pool size is a band-aid if the real problem is one query hogging connections for too long, and can push too many connections onto the database itself

Mentions adding monitoring/alerting on pool utilization so this is caught before it causes user-facing timeouts next time
